sp.p: Faculty, yup. And then you went to Hunter Liggett from there, from Leavenworth? Leonard Morley: No. We went to Washington.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: No. We went to Washington.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: Went to Washington again. And then you ended up out at Hunter Liggett?

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: No, we didn't go to Washington. We went to Hunter Liggett.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: That's what I'm thinking. So you went on to Hunter Liggett, which Hunter Liggett is a military reservation that reports in to Fort Ord, California, and what's the purpose of Hunter Liggett?

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: Well, it was training.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: Training. Okay. And as I understand it, it's kind of out in the middle of nowhere, is that correct?

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: It's a lot of acreage.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: Lot of acreage, yup, and there's a place -- But you were the post commander, correct, Len was?

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: Len was.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: You're the wife of the post commander. You're a full colonel and --

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: I wasn't a full colonel.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: Well, you're the wife of a full colonel, and so I want to get your experiences because there was also hunting that was done out at Hunter Liggett.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: And tell me about the day you had 17 stars in your kitchen.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: Well, there was a large community of retired officers in the Monterey area, and when fall came and dove season and deer season came, they all wanted to come down to hunt. And, of course, this was the former ranch property that was adjacent to and belonged to Hearst, adjacent to the San Simeon property. And the building -- the main building was called the hacienda, and it had been used as the ranch headquarters, and there were cowboy rooms, and there were some apartment areas that were or suites that guests stayed in. And the kitchen that I had was very -- it was large but not commodious. Anyhow, there was not a messing facility, and particularly when they wanted to be out before dawn, and so when we first got there, I elected myself to fix breakfast. And there was a big pot of oatmeal, eggs any style, buckwheat cakes I raised every night with yeast, and pitchers of orange juice, and they all could help themselves. And one day I counted and there were 17 stars in that kitchen all helping themselves. Well, at that point we hadn't met any of the wives or anything, and I was -- every time I'd meet one, Oh, you're the one that makes the buckwheat cakes. So we --

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: Well, tell me who these 17 stars are. You had General Omar Bradley who had five stars.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: No, he wasn't there for hunting.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: He wasn't there for that one?

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: He came by himself.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: Oh, he came by himself. Tell me about who, do you recall who the 17 stars were?

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: General Freeman.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: General Freeman.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: General McNaughton. I don't -- you're asking --

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: I'm asking tough times, but anyway, you had enough generals there to count up to 17 stars. Okay. So you met General MacArthur in Japan or Len has, and then you went to his funeral in Washington.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: We met Mrs. MacArthur many times.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: Met Mrs. MacArthur many times. And General Bradley came himself to Hunter Liggett.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: And came to lunch with you.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: I had dinner for him.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: Dinner for him.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: I fixed soup, two different kinds of soup and salad materials. And they sent an aide from Fort Ord, and there was an apartment, a suite upstairs from us, and so the aide fixed us lunch when he came. And that evening we had he and his aide, General Moore.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: General Hal Moore.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: Hal Moore.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: Okay.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: And his deputy, Jack -- oh, Mary, my memory at this point. Anyhow, there were eight of us for dinner that evening. Two, four, six. Pardon me. And I fixed prime rib, I made apple pie, tossed salad. I don't know what all I fixed. And he was a wonderful conversationalist.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: You know, everybody said General Omar Bradley is a soldier's general. Is that your impression?

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: Indeed. And when he came in, I have a picture that was taken in Japan when he came to inspect the troops. General MacArthur did not go out a lot socially, very seldom. Leonard Morley: He went out that time.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: But he and General Bradley were reviewing the troops on the parade grounds at the Imperial Palace, and as they were coming from the reviewing stand, this picture was snapped. So when General Bradley came, I got the scrapbook out and asked him if he would autograph it for me, and he did.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: Nice.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: We had a lovely dinner and conversation.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: Okay. So then you retired, Len retired from the Army when?

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: We were at Hunter Liggett for six years. In June of 1976.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: June of '76, and you moved to where? Leonard Morley: Fort Lewis.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: No. We moved to Salkum, Washington.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: Salkum, Washington. Leonard Morley: Well, I retired at Fort Lewis.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: You retired at Fort Lewis, and then you moved to Salkum. Did you buy that then or had you bought that place before? Leonard Morley: We bought it a year before we retired.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: Before.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: So you are now, it's 1976 and here it is 2002, you're still living there.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: So you have lived there for 26 years. Leonard Morley: 26 years.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: Anything that comes to mind as we wrap this thing up, we've gone pretty close to our 90 minutes. So what's your reflections on your life as a soldier, I call you a soldier with great respect, I don't know whether you call yourself or not, but I call you a soldier because you served in two wars, and as a soldier's wife, what's your -- what's your reflections on that? Anything to wrap it up?

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: All I hope is that I served my country well and that I was a good representative of our nation.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: I'll tell you what my experience was. You were outstanding. Thank you very much, Chartley.

sp.speaker: Chartley M. Morley
sp.p: You're welcome.

sp.speaker: Robert Babcock
sp.p: This has been very informative. [Interview concluded]
